# test/fixtures/90.05-tapes/ — provenance and reconstruction notes

*Created 2026-09-13, M6 stage 1. These are the two input tapes of the
J28-6169 Appendix 90.05 sample payroll program, reconstructed from its
printed report. The manual prints the report, PDF p. 217, and not the
tapes that produced it.*

## What the directory holds

| File | Unit | The sample's file | Content |
|---|---|---|---|
| `D1.tap` | `D1` | INPUTMASTER | 25 master records, 15 words each, in one block of 20 records and one block of 5 |
| `C2.tap` | `C2` | DETAILFILE | 14 detail records, one 3-word record in the first portion of each 14-word block |

Both are SIMH `.tap` images in the M5-2 frame (`docs/design/m5-io.md`).
`tool/generate_sample_tapes.dart` writes them from the table in
`tool/sample_tapes_source.dart`. Do not edit the images by hand. The
golden test `test/sample_tapes_test.dart` regenerates them and compares
the bytes.

The run writes its five output tapes into the same directory, so copy
the directory before a run:

```sh
cp -r test/fixtures/90.05-tapes /tmp/tapes
dart run comtran:comtranc test/fixtures/90.05-payroll-job.ctd --run --tapes=/tmp/tapes --list-tapes
```

## The evidence

The page is `comtran-manuals/J28-6169/images/page-217.png`. It holds four
reports: PAYFILE in full, CHECKFILE in part (the last three of eleven
checks), BONDORDERFILE in full (one order), and ERRORFILE in full (17
lines). The scan is ground truth (CLAUDE.md section 9). Two facts about
the page govern its reading:

- **The print is skewed.** Every line rises to the right by about one
  line height across the page width. The right-hand amount fields of a
  PAYFILE line therefore sit one row above its left-hand text. They lie
  on one straight tilted baseline. The transcription in
  `comtran-manuals/J28-6169/90.05-sample-program.md` assigned those
  fields to the row above and described the result as a printer
  practice. It is the skew. Jack authorized the correction on
  2026-09-14, and the transcription now reads each line along its own
  baseline. Three cells of its block still differed from the scan.
  Jack authorized those on 2026-09-15, and the block now prints them
  (`docs/design/m6-acceptance.md` M6-2). Read each line along
  its own baseline. The
  first PAYFILE line ends `2.00  2.00  112.20` with no bond
  denomination. The GT line ends `28.00  28.00  2180.63  37.50`. The
  arithmetic of every line confirms the reading (below).
- **The print chain renders some letters O as C.** The BONDORDERFILE
  line prints the name `WCO J`. The same master NAME field prints
  `WOO J` on the PAYFILE line and on the check, so the field is `WOO J`
  and the bond-order print is an artifact. Two ERRORFILE names print
  `MOCRE`, with no second print to compare. They are keyed as the ink
  reads.

## How each field was derived

The program is the deck `90.05-payroll.ct`. The report fixes a master
field through the statements that print it:

| Field | Derivation |
|---|---|
| EMPLOYEE.NUMBER, NAME | The PAYFILE line prints both. An ERRORFILE `M` line prints both for an unmatched master. |
| RATE | GROSS = HOURS × RATE (statement 210, the OTHERWISE arm). No line exceeds 40 hours, so the overtime arm never runs. RATE = GROSS ÷ HOURS, exact in every case. |
| EXEMPTIONS | WHT = 0.18 × (GROSS − 13 × EXEMPTIONS), rounded (statement 215). One integer satisfies each line. |
| FICA, year to date | Statement 212 adds 3% of GROSS to the master's FICA. Statement 213 caps the master at 144.00 and takes the excess off the pay. A printed FICA of 0.00 needs the master at exactly 144.00 before the add. DORR's 2.01 = 144.00 − 141.99. CASPERIAN's 3.20 is the full 3%, so the master held any value up to 140.80; 0.00 is chosen. |
| BONDEDUCTION | The PAYFILE prints it (statement 218). A blank is a zero, which skips BOND.ROUTINE (statement 216). |
| BONDENOMINATION, BONDACCUMULATION | WOO's order prints 37.50, so the denomination is 37.50 and the accumulation plus 17.00 reached it: 20.50 is chosen, the least value that orders. SOBEK, REYNOLDS and WILLIAMS deduct and order nothing, so the denomination exceeds the accumulation plus the deduction: 18.75, a $25 bond, and 0.00 are chosen. |
| DATE | Statement 209 overwrites it with the detail date before anything prints it. Blank. |
| TRIGGERS; GROSS, RETIREMENT, INSURANCE and WHT year to date | Added to, never printed. Blank and zero. |

An unmatched master takes its number and name from its ERRORFILE line
and zero or blank in every other field.

A detail record is its number, the date `100661` and the hours. A
matched detail takes its hours from the PAYFILE HRS column. An unmatched
detail prints whole on its ERRORFILE `D` line.

Three details match no master. Each prints whole on its ERRORFILE line:
`061500` with 400 hours, `071899` with 400, and `091983` with 400.

The arithmetic check of each PAYFILE line, NETPAY = GROSS − FICA − WHT −
INS.PREM − RET.PREM − BONDEDUCTION, holds on every line as the page
prints it. The department totals are the sums of their lines. The GT
line is the sum of the department totals in every column but one:
the printed net pay, 2180.63, is 3.20 below the sum of the printed
department nets, 2183.83. `docs/design/m6-acceptance.md` records the
difference.

## The word layout

A master record is the 15 words of [J 90.05.02]: the number, three
words of name and triggers, then RATE, DATE, EXEMPTIONS, GROSS,
RETIREMENT, INSURANCE, FICA, WHT, BONDEDUCTION, BONDACCUMULATION and
BONDENOMINATION. A character field is six BCD characters to the word
(D0.6). An internal field is the binary integer of its digits, the
decimal point implied. A detail record is three words: the number, the
date, and the three characters of HOURS followed by three blanks
([J 90.05.03]). The other eleven words of its block are blank, as a
card-to-tape pass leaves them.
